question: Tattvabodhini Patrika promoted the study of India’s past in which language?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengali**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tattvabodhini Patrika** promoted the study of India's past in the **Bengali** language.
 
• The journal was a significant publication of the **Tattvabodhini Sabha**, which was founded by **Debendranath Tagore** in 1839.
 
• Tattvabodhini Patrika played a crucial role in the **Bengali Renaissance**, encouraging the spread of new ideas and the study of Indian heritage and culture.
 
• The Patrika not only focused on the past but also discussed contemporary social and religious issues, aiming at the reformation of society.
 
• It was instrumental in the intellectual and cultural awakening of Bengal during the 19th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Debendranath Tagore**, the father of the famous poet **Rabindranath Tagore**, was a leading figure of the Bengal Renaissance and a key proponent of the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• The **Brahmo Samaj** was a reformist movement within Hinduism that aimed at monotheism and opposed idolatry and superstitions.
 
• The **Tattvabodhini Sabha** was initially formed to rejuvenate the Brahmo Samaj and later expanded its focus to cultural and educational activities.
 
• Through publications like Tattvabodhini Patrika, the Sabha sought to educate the masses and promote rational thinking.
 
• The journal continued to be influential until the early 20th century, reflecting the changing socio-political landscape of India.
